facts.text: The only player of the 2000s to shoot .950 from the line in a single postseason (60+ FTA): Peja Stojakovic, 2000-01 — .968 on 62 FTA.
The only player of the 2000s to average 2 steals and 2 blocks (60% of games): Gerald Wallace, 2005-06 — 2.5 spg, 2.1 bpg.
Only two players of the 2000s shot 50-40-90 (min. 100 3PA, 125 FTA, 60% of games): Steve Nash (4×, best 2007-08: .504/.470/.906); Dirk Nowitzki (2006-07: .502/.416/.904).
The only player of the 2000s to average a triple-double in a single postseason (8+ playoff games): Jason Kidd, 2006-07 — 14.6/10.9/10.9.
The only player of the 2000s to attempt 2,000 field goals in a season: Kobe Bryant, 2005-06 — 2,173 FGA.
The only player of the 2000s to average 20 points and 10 assists (60% of games) was Chris Paul — and he did it twice (2008-09: 22.8 ppg, 11.0 apg; 2007-08: 21.1 ppg, 11.6 apg).
The only player of the 2000s to make 700 free throws in a season: Kevin Durant, 2009-10 — 756 FTM.
The only player of the 2000s to average 10 rebounds and 2 steals (60% of games): Shawn Marion, 2004-05 — 11.3 rpg, 2.0 spg.

The only player of the 2000s to average 30 points on under .450 shooting (60% of games) was Allen Iverson — and he did it 4 times (2001-02: 31.4 ppg, .398 FG; 2005-06: 33.0 ppg, .447 FG; 2000-01: 31.1 ppg, .420 FG; …).
The only player of the 2000s to grab more offensive rebounds than defensive (300+ reb): Jason Maxiell, 2008-09 — 169 off, 155 def.
Only two players of the 2000s shot .600 from the field on 800+ attempts: Dwight Howard (2×, best 2009-10: .612 on 834 FGA); Shaquille O'Neal (3×, best 2008-09: .609 on 841 FGA).
Only two players of the 2000s averaged 20 points, 10 rebounds and 5 assists (60% of games): Kevin Garnett (3×, best 2002-03: 23.0/13.4/6.0); Chris Webber (2002-03: 23.0/10.5/5.4).
Tim Duncan averaged a double-digit rebounding figure in 10 straight seasons (2000-01 to 2009-10), the longest run of the 2000s.
Jason Kidd averaged 8+ assists in 10 straight seasons (2000-01 to 2009-10), the longest run of the 2000s.
Kobe Bryant averaged 20+ points in 10 straight seasons (2000-01 to 2009-10), the longest run of the 2000s.
Only two players of the 2000s recorded 200 steals in a season: Allen Iverson (2002-03: 225 stl); Chris Paul (2×, best 2007-08: 217 stl).

Just four players of the 2000s shot .900 from the line on 400+ attempts: Kevin Durant (2009-10: .900 on 840 FTA); Dirk Nowitzki (3×, best 2009-10: .915 on 586 FTA); Chauncey Billups (3×, best 2009-10: .910 on 512 FTA); Peja Stojakovic (2003-04: .927 on 425 FTA).
Only two players of the 2000s averaged 25 points while missing 40% of the season (20+ games): Allen Iverson (2003-04: 26.4 ppg in 48 games); Yao Ming (2006-07: 25.0 ppg in 48 games).
Only two players of the 2000s recorded more assists than points (60% of games, 300+ ast): Chris Childs (2001-02: 351 ast, 285 pts); Mark Jackson (2000-01: 661 ast, 631 pts).

Just four players of the 2000s shot .560 or better while averaging 20 points (60% of games): Shaquille O'Neal (6×, best 2000-01: .572 FG, 28.7 ppg); Amar'e Stoudemire (2×, best 2007-08: .590 FG, 25.2 ppg); Dwight Howard (2×, best 2007-08: .599 FG, 20.7 ppg); Carlos Boozer (2006-07: .561 FG, 20.9 ppg).
Kobe Bryant averaged 25+ points in 6 straight seasons (2004-05 to 2009-10), the longest run of the 2000s.
LeBron James scored 2,000 points in 6 straight seasons (2004-05 to 2009-10), the longest run of the 2000s.
Shaquille O'Neal shot .500 from the field (800+ FGA) in 6 straight seasons (2000-01 to 2005-06), the longest run of the 2000s.

Just four players of the 2000s shot under .550 from the line on 300+ attempts: Shaquille O'Neal (5×, best 2000-01: .513 on 972 FTA); Ben Wallace (2004-05: .428 on 304 FTA); Antoine Walker (2004-05: .539 on 373 FTA); Jamaal Magloire (2005-06: .535 on 333 FTA).

Just four players of the 2000s averaged 25 points, 5 rebounds and 5 assists (60% of games): LeBron James (6×, best 2009-10: 29.7/7.3/8.6); Tracy McGrady (4×, best 2002-03: 32.1/6.5/5.5); Kobe Bryant (6×, best 2002-03: 30.0/6.9/5.9); Dwyane Wade (2×, best 2008-09: 30.2/5.0/7.5).
Ray Allen shot .900 from the line (200+ FTA) in 5 straight seasons (2005-06 to 2009-10), the longest run of the 2000s.
Derek Fisher played every game in 5 straight seasons (2005-06 to 2009-10), the longest run of the 2000s.
Marcus Camby averaged 2.5+ blocks in 5 straight seasons (2003-04 to 2007-08), the longest run of the 2000s.
Ray Allen made 150+ threes in 5 straight seasons (2004-05 to 2008-09), the longest run of the 2000s.

Just four players of the 2000s averaged 3 blocks a game (60% of games): Theo Ratliff (3×, best 2000-01: 3.7 bpg); Marcus Camby (4×, best 2007-08: 3.6 bpg); Ben Wallace (3×, best 2001-02: 3.5 bpg); Andrei Kirilenko (2005-06: 3.2 bpg).

Just four players of the 2000s scored 600 points in one postseason: Allen Iverson (2000-01: 723 pts in 22 games); Kobe Bryant (3×, best 2008-09: 695 pts in 23 games); Dwyane Wade (2005-06: 654 pts in 23 games); Dirk Nowitzki (2005-06: 620 pts in 23 games).

Just four players of the 2000s averaged 30 points in a single postseason (8+ playoff games): LeBron James (2×, best 2008-09: 35.3 ppg in 14 games); Allen Iverson (2×, best 2000-01: 32.9 ppg in 22 games); Kobe Bryant (3×, best 2002-03: 32.1 ppg in 12 games); Shaquille O'Neal (2000-01: 30.4 ppg in 16 games).
Just three players of the 2000s blocked 250 shots in a season: Theo Ratliff (2×, best 2003-04: 307 blk); Marcus Camby (2007-08: 285 blk); Ben Wallace (2001-02: 278 blk).

Just three players of the 2000s averaged 20 points and 10 rebounds with under 1.5 assists (60% of games): Dwight Howard (2×, best 2007-08: 20.7/14.2/1.3); Al Jefferson (2007-08: 21.0/11.1/1.4); Yao Ming (2005-06: 22.3/10.2/1.5).
Most assists in a single postseason in the 2000s: Rajon Rondo, 2009-10 — 223 in 24 games.
Most rebounds in a single postseason in the 2000s: Tim Duncan, 2002-03 — 369 in 24 games.
Lowest field-goal percentage by a 20-point scorer in the 2000s: Antoine Walker, 2002-03 — .388 while averaging 20.1.
Best free-throw percentage on 500+ attempts in the 2000s: Dirk Nowitzki, 2009-10 — .915 (536-586).
Most assists by a sub-10-point scorer in the 2000s: Jason Kidd, 2008-09 — 702 assists while averaging 9.0.
Most personal fouls in a season in the 2000s: Kurt Thomas, 2002-03 — 344.
Most assists in a season in the 2000s: Chris Paul, 2007-08 — 925 (11.6 a game).
Most rebounds by a sub-10-point scorer in the 2000s: Ben Wallace, 2002-03 — 1,126 rebounds while averaging 6.9.
Highest assist average of the 2000s: Steve Nash, 2006-07 — 11.6 a game.
Best free-throw percentage in a season (125+ made) in the 2000s: Jose Calderon, 2008-09 — .981.
Most free throws made in a season in the 2000s: Kevin Durant, 2009-10 — 756 of 840.
Most offensive rebounds in a season in the 2000s: Elton Brand, 2001-02 — 396.
Most blocked shots in a season in the 2000s: Theo Ratliff, 2003-04 — 307.
Most threes attempted while shooting under .330 from deep in the 2000s: Antoine Walker, 2002-03 — 582 attempts at .323.
Best three-point percentage on 300+ attempts in the 2000s: Joe Johnson, 2004-05 — .478 (177-370).
Most threes made in a season in the 2000s: Ray Allen, 2005-06 — 269.
Metta World Peace averaged 2+ steals in 4 straight seasons (2000-01 to 2003-04), the longest run of the 2000s.
Most points in a single postseason in the 2000s: Allen Iverson, 2000-01 — 723 in 22 games.
Best field-goal percentage in a postseason (150+ FGA) in the 2000s: Shaquille O'Neal, 2005-06 — .612.
Most rebounds in a season in the 2000s: Dwight Howard, 2007-08 — 1,161 (14.2 a game).
Highest rebounding average of the 2000s: Ben Wallace, 2002-03 — 15.4 a game.
7 player-seasons of the 2000s ended on 9.9 rebounds a game, a tenth short of a double-digit average — among them Dirk Nowitzki (2002-03), Shawn Marion (2001-02), Donyell Marshall (2003-04).
7 player-seasons of the 2000s ended on a .399 three-point percentage (200+ 3PA), one point short of .400 — among them Dirk Nowitzki (2004-05), Derek Anderson (2000-01), Metta World Peace (2008-09).
Most rebounds of the 2000s: Tim Duncan, 8,869.
Most assists of the 2000s: Steve Nash, 7,506.
Most games played in the 2000s: Andre Miller, 815.
Most personal fouls committed in the 2000s: Kurt Thomas, 2,446.
2005-06 had 10 25-point scorers, the most of any season in the 2000s.
2003-04 had just one 25-point scorer, the fewest of any season in the 2000s.
2000-01 had 6 20-and-10 players, the most of any season in the 2000s.
2004-05 had just 3 20-and-10 players, the fewest of any season in the 2000s.
2002-03 had 5 .900 free-throw shooters (200+ FTA), the most of any season in the 2000s.
2001-02 had just one .900 free-throw shooter (200+ FTA), the fewest of any season in the 2000s.
2001-02 had 7 8-assist players, the most of any season in the 2000s.
2003-04 had just 3 8-assist players, the fewest of any season in the 2000s.
2007-08 had 31 20-point scorers, the most of any season in the 2000s.
2009-10 had just 17 20-point scorers, the fewest of any season in the 2000s.
2007-08 had 43 players who appeared in every game, the most of any season in the 2000s.
2000-01 had just one player who appeared in every game, the fewest of any season in the 2000s.
2007-08 had 14 double-digit rebounders, the most of any season in the 2000s.
2001-02 had just 9 double-digit rebounders, the fewest of any season in the 2000s.
Most steals of the 2000s: Jason Kidd, 1,483.
Most blocked shots of the 2000s: Tim Duncan, 1,738.
Most threes of the 2000s: Ray Allen, 1,947.
Most turnovers of the 2000s: Steve Nash, 2,481.
2005-06 had 3 30-point scorers, the most of any season in the 2000s.
2003-04 had no 30-point scorers at all — the only season of the 2000s without one.
2000-01 had 7 2-steal players, the most of any season in the 2000s.
2008-09 had just 2 2-steal players, the fewest of any season in the 2000s.
3 player-seasons of the 2000s ended on a .499 field-goal percentage (800+ FGA), one point short of .500 — among them Kevin Garnett (2003-04), Tim Duncan (2000-01), Brook Lopez (2009-10).
39 players made 150 threes at a .400 clip in the 2000s (60 seasons). The most extreme: Ray Allen, 2005-06 — 269 3PM, .412.
29 players grabbed more rebounds than they scored points (60% of games, 500+ reb) in the 2000s (61 seasons). The most extreme: Ben Wallace, 2002-03 — 1,126 reb, 506 pts.
Exactly one player of the 2000s finished a season with a 24.9 scoring average, a tenth short of 25: Antawn Jamison (2000-01).
Exactly one player of the 2000s finished a season with 9.9 assists a game, a tenth short of 10: Jason Kidd (2001-02).
6 players shot .450 from three on 250+ attempts in the 2000s (8 seasons). The most extreme: Joe Johnson, 2004-05 — .478 on 370 3PA.
6 players grabbed 1,000 rebounds in a season in the 2000s (16 seasons). The most extreme: Dwight Howard, 2007-08 — 1,161 reb.
5 players dished out 800 assists in a season in the 2000s (11 seasons). The most extreme: Chris Paul, 2007-08 — 925 ast.
6 players averaged 9+ assists (60% of games) in the 2000s (20 seasons). The most extreme: Steve Nash, 2006-07 — 11.6 apg.
5 players averaged 10 assists a game (60% of games) in the 2000s (12 seasons). The most extreme: Steve Nash, 2006-07 — 11.6 apg.
10 players committed 300 personal fouls in a season in the 2000s (12 seasons). The most extreme: Kurt Thomas, 2002-03 — 344 PF.
5 players blocked more shots than they assisted while averaging 20 points (60% of games) in the 2000s (11 seasons). The most extreme: Dwight Howard, 2008-09 — 231 blk, 112 ast.
5 players averaged 2.5 steals a game (60% of games) in the 2000s (8 seasons). The most extreme: Larry Hughes, 2004-05 — 2.9 spg.
11 players averaged 20+ points with fewer than 2 assists a game (60% of games) in the 2000s (21 seasons). The most extreme: Amar'e Stoudemire, 2009-10 — 23.1 ppg, 1.0 apg.
5 players made 150+ threes while shooting under .340 from deep in the 2000s (6 seasons). The most extreme: Baron Davis, 2003-04 — 187 3PM, .321.
12 players shot better from three than from two (250+ 3PA, 300+ 2PA) in the 2000s. The most extreme: Chauncey Billups, 2005-06 — .433 3P, .407 2P.
45 players shot under .440 on 1,200+ attempts in the 2000s (78 seasons). The most extreme: Jerry Stackhouse, 2000-01 — .402 on 1,927 FGA.

method: Every player's regular-season and playoff totals for every season in the decade, pulled from stats.nba.com, the league's official record. Nothing is recalled or estimated; the rows behind each line are stored with it.
Qualification is 60% of the most games anyone played that season. Attempt floors are stated in the line.
Categories not yet recorded (rebounds before 1950-51, minutes before 1951-52, steals and blocks before 1973-74, turnovers before 1977-78, threes before 1979-80) are treated as missing, never as zero.
Team-mate lines are omitted: the feed credits a traded player's whole season to one club.
